name: shiftwork_plan
title: Shift work: plan
description: Shift-work plan: which units of a checkpoint may run NOW, and in what waves — the batches its `depends_on` graph permits, computed read-only from the file. Call it before dispatching a wave: `ready` (the first batch) is what shiftwork_clock_in will brief, and `width` is how many agents the widest wave needs. A `ready` member beyond the cursor is clockable only once clock-in has briefed it; without that brief, clock-out refuses it. Use shiftwork_status instead when you only want progress counts, and work_plan when the graph is yours to hand over as `nodes` rather than a checkpoint on disk — this tool reads the checkpoint's own plan.units. Units already `done` or `dropped` count as satisfied and are left out of every batch; `todo`, `in_progress` and `blocked` stay in. Order inside a batch is plan.units order, because the checkpoint schema has no priority field. It never moves plan.cursor — the cursor is echoed unchanged so the pointer and the batch view can be read side by side — and never writes anything. Refusals are structured, never exceptions: work_plan's sentences for a duplicate id, an unknown dependency or a cycle, and shiftwork_status's for a checkpoint it cannot read; a plan whose units are all terminal answers an empty `ready`, which is an answer, not a refusal. It reports logical order only: `depends_on` says nothing about two units writing the same file, so the orchestrator still decides what actually runs together.

checkpoint.title: Checkpoint
checkpoint.description: Path to the shift-work checkpoint JSON file (by convention .shiftwork/checkpoint.json in the repo the job works on), absolute or relative to the server's working directory. The same file shiftwork_plan, shiftwork_clock_in and shiftwork_clock_out take; it must validate against assets/schemas/shiftwork-checkpoint.json.

result.description: `plan` on success; `error` with `reason` when the checkpoint cannot be read or its graph cannot batch.

batches.description: Unit ids by wave: batch k holds every non-terminal unit whose dependencies all sit in batches below k.

ready.description: batches[0] — the units clock_in may brief now; [] when every unit is done or dropped.

width.description: The largest batch length: the widest fan-out.

reason.description: With result `error`: one sentence saying why the call was refused.
